query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Clear ordinal categories (excellent/good/acceptable/poor) describing a specific product attribute; well-separated and segmentable against satisfaction.

per_column.name: product_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: A generic overall quality assessment is essentially a proxy/restatement of satisfaction itself rather than an external product attribute, so it risks trivial correlation.

per_column.name: freshness_delivery_condition
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories (fresh/damaged/stale) capturing a distinct delivery/condition attribute; segmentable, though ~39% NULL weakens coverage.

per_column.name: ingredient_quality_naturalness
per_column.rationale: Distinct attribute about naturalness/health concerns with well-separated categories that can be compared against satisfaction.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Price-value dimension with clear ordered categories; a classic, interpretable driver to segment satisfaction on and distinct from the focus.

per_column.name: product_consistency_reliability
per_column.rationale: Consistency/reliability attribute with graded categories; interpretable and distinct from overall satisfaction.

per_column.name: competitive_product_standing
per_column.rationale: Relative positioning against competitors with clear categories; an external associational variable segmentable against satisfaction.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repeat-purchase intent is an outcome/consequence of satisfaction, not a product attribute; correlating it with satisfaction is near-tautological rather than explanatory.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are genuine, interpretable product-attribute dimensions (taste, freshness, ingredients, value, consistency, competitive standing) with well-separated categorical scales that a human can segment on and compare against satisfaction, directly serving the query about attributes associated with satisfaction. Two columns weaken the set: product_quality_assessment is an overall quality proxy that largely restates satisfaction, and repeat_purchase_intent is a downstream outcome rather than an attribute, so both invite trivial/tautological correlations. Some columns carry substantial NULL rates (freshness ~39%, value/ingredients/consistency ~10-15%), reducing comparison power but not eliminating it. Overall this is a strong, human-interpretable EDA schema with a couple of restatement-type inclusions.
